transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, welcome! Watch your step, mind the sparks. Just pulling out this last batch of iron from the coals. Can I help you with something, ma'am? The master isn't in today, I'm afraid. He's... well, he's off on a sourcing trip, out in the mountains. Won't be back for weeks, probably.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I see... That's rather unfortunate timing. I actually came to discuss a sword that was recently commissioned. It's... not quite up to the standards I had expected. I was hoping to speak with the master about a remake.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Oh, a remake? Hmm. Well, I'm sorry to hear it's not what you expected, ma'am. But... all commissioned Nichirin swords are final sale, per guild tradition. And even a Hashira must wait three months for any reforging request to be considered. It's just how things are done. The master made that quite clear to me before he left. He said, "No exceptions, lad, not even for the strongest." So, I really can't help you with a remake right now, even if the master *were* here, which he isn't.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand the guild's tradition, but the issue is not with the quality of the craftsmanship itself. The blade is warped, and it won't hold its shape during practice swings. This is a functional issue, not a matter of personal preference. I would like to discuss this with the master when he returns, if possible. Is there any way to leave a message or arrange a meeting upon his return?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
A warped blade, you say? Hmm, that does sound like a problem. Not ideal at all for a Hashira, or anyone for that matter. Still, the policy's the policy, ma'am. It's not something I can override, especially with the master gone.

As for leaving a message... I can certainly write it down for him when he eventually gets back. I'll stick it right here on his workbench, where he can't miss it. But I can't promise when he'll see it, and like I said, he won't be back for weeks. He's quite thorough on these trips. No birds, no runners, no way to reach him 'til he's back at the forge door.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I see... I understand that the situation is not ideal for either party. I will wait for the master's return, then. Please ensure that my message is delivered promptly. In the meantime, I should continue with my training. Is there any advice you can offer to help me compensate for the... malfunctions of the current blade?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Compensate for malfunctions... hmm. That's a tricky one, ma'am. A warped blade is always a nuisance. For training, I'd say be extra careful with your swings, especially any that put torque on the blade. You don't want to make the warp worse, or worse yet, have it snap.

Perhaps focus on forms that rely less on brute force and more on precision and footwork for a while? Or, if you have a training dummy, perhaps use a wooden practice sword for your more vigorous exercises until the master can take a look at yours. It's not ideal, I know, but it might save your real blade from further damage, and you from potential injury. We wouldn't want that.

I'll definitely make sure he gets your message the moment he steps back through that door. Until then, please be careful.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Thank you for the advice. It's not ideal, but it is sound counsel. I will focus on precision and footwork, and use a wooden practice sword for more vigorous exercises. Your concern is much appreciated.

Regarding the message, I would like to add that the issue with the blade is not merely cosmetic. As a Hashira, my ability to perform my duties could be compromised if I were to use a faulty weapon in a real-world scenario. This is not just a personal inconvenience; it could potentially affect the outcome of critical missions. I trust the master will take this into consideration when he reviews the message.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Understood, ma'am. That's a very serious point, indeed. A Hashira's duties are paramount, and a faulty weapon is a danger to everyone. I'll make sure to write *all* of that down for the master, exactly as you've said it – that this isn't just a matter of preference, but one that could compromise your ability to perform your crucial duties. He'll understand the gravity of it.

I'll pin it right where he prepares his coals, so it'll be the first thing he sees when he returns. But truly, there's no way to reach him before then. He's quite thorough on these trips. Just know that your message, with all its importance, will be waiting for him.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I'm grateful for your understanding and assistance. I know the master is a skilled artisan, and I trust he will address this matter with the seriousness it deserves. In the meantime, I will do everything in my power to maintain my fitness and sharpness with the makeshift arrangements you've suggested. Please pass along my thanks for your time and attention to this matter. I hope the master's trip is successful and that he returns safely.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
You're most welcome, ma'am. I'm just doing my part to keep things running while the master's away. I'll make sure he gets your full message, and I'll emphasize everything you've said about the seriousness of the issue and your duties.

I hope his trip is successful too. He always brings back the best materials. Thank you for stopping by, and please do be careful with that blade. We'll get this sorted out when he returns. Safe travels, ma'am.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you once more. I will indeed be cautious. Safe travels to you as well, and may your work here be productive and rewarding. I'll return when the master is available, and I'm confident that we'll be able to resolve this matter to everyone's satisfaction. Wishing you a pleasant day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: And to you as well, ma'am! It was... well, it was certainly a conversation. I'll be here, keeping the fires stoked. You have a pleasant day too. And don't you worry, that message will be waiting for him. Safe travels!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: To you too, kind artisan. I will be back when the time is right. Until then, may your work be well and may we both find success in our respective paths. Take care.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Farewell, ma'am! I'll be here. And I'll make sure the message is waiting, clear as day. Take care yourself, and may your training go well despite the circumstances. Until next time!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Farewell! Your dedication to your craft is evident, and I have no doubt that the master's absence is a testament to that. I will take your words to heart, and I will be back. May fortune favor us both.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Understood, ma'am. I appreciate that. Keeping the forge running is important work. I'll be here, hammering away. And the master will get your message the moment he's back. May fortune favor us both! Safe journey!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Safe journey to you as well. I'll be on my way, with a heart full of hope and a mind set on the tasks ahead. May we both find what we seek in the time to come. Take care, and I look forward to our next meeting.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Farewell, ma'am! And good luck with your training. I'll make sure everything is ready for the master when he finally returns. You take care, and I look forward to your next visit. Until then!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Farewell! Your support is greatly appreciated. I will press on with my training, and I'm certain that when we next meet, it will be under better circumstances. May the forge's fires burn brightly in your hands. Until we meet again!

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: She strongly emphasizes her duties as a Hashira, stating the faulty weapon could compromise critical missions, indicating a high sense of responsibility and purpose.
